chunks: Ma'ani al-Akhbar: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Khashab, from Ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whatever you find in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then acting upon it is incumbent upon you; you have no excuse for abandoning it …
ai.seo_question: What is the basis for acting upon Quranic verses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, underscores the Quran's role as the definitive and self-sufficient source of legislation, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence. It emphasizes that the divine text is comprehensive enough to provide binding rulings for all aspects of life, leaving no room for valid excuse in neglecting its clear directives.

en.ammaar-muslim: 13. [13/-] Ma’ani al-Akhbar: Ibn al-Walid from al-Saffar from al-Khashab from Ibn Kalub from Ishaq b. Ammar from Ja’far from his forefathers عليهم السلام: the messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:
whatever you find in the Book of Allah Mighty and Majestic then acting is to be based upon it and you have no excuse to abandon it …
